1|- BREAKING: [Decoders now accept all well-formed simple values](https://github.com/PJK/libcbor/pull/445)
2|  - Previously, `cbor_load` and `cbor_stream_decode` rejected the unassigned simple values 0 to 19 (`0xE0` to `0xF3`) and 32 to 255 (`0xF8 0x20` to `0xF8 0xFF`) with `CBOR_ERR_MALFORMATED` / `CBOR_DECODER_ERROR`, even though RFC 8949 Section 3.3 defines them as well-formed and `cbor_build_ctrl` could already produce them. They are now decoded into ctrl items readable through `cbor_ctrl_value`. `0xF8` followed by a byte below `0x20` remains a well-formedness error as specified
3|  - New `simple_value` member appended to `struct cbor_callbacks` and a matching `cbor_null_simple_value_callback` no-op. Like all other members, it must be set: existing callback sets that do not initialize it (e.g. designated initializers that predate the member) will dereference `NULL` on such input. Use `cbor_null_simple_value_callback` to ignore these values, or start from `cbor_empty_callbacks`
4|  - Discovered by running the [CBOR Working Group test vectors](https://github.com/cbor-wg/cbor-test-vectors) (`rfc8949-appendixA/mt7-simple`)

1|Simple values
2|~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
3|
4|`RFC 8949 Section 3.3 <https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8949#section-3.3>`_ defines
5|simple values 0 to 255, of which only ``false`` (20), ``true`` (21), ``null`` (22),
6|and ``undefined`` (23) are assigned. *libcbor* represents all of them as ctrl items:
7|:func:`cbor_ctrl_value` returns the raw value, and :func:`cbor_is_bool`,
8|:func:`cbor_is_null`, and :func:`cbor_is_undef` identify the assigned ones.
9|
10|The unassigned values 0 to 19 and 32 to 255 are well-formed and are decoded and
11|encoded as-is. Values 24 to 31 are reserved and cannot be represented in well-formed
12|CBOR; the decoders reject them, and :func:`cbor_build_ctrl` will produce an encoding
13|that other decoders will reject as well.

230|struct cbor_decoder_result {
231|  /** Input bytes read/consumed
232|   *
233|   * If this is less than the size of input buffer, the client will likely
234|   * resume parsing starting at the next byte (e.g. `buffer + result.read`).
235|   *
236|   * Set to 0 if the #status is not #CBOR_DECODER_FINISHED.
237|   */
238|  size_t read;
239|
240|  /** The decoding status */
241|  enum cbor_decoder_status status;
242|
243|  /** Number of bytes needed in the input buffer to make progress
244|   *
245|   * Set to 0 unless the result status is #CBOR_DECODER_NEDATA. When it is:
246|   *  - #required is the total number of bytes that must be present at the
247|   *    start of the buffer before calling #cbor_stream_decode again will
248|   *    invoke a callback. The caller should accumulate bytes until at least
249|   *    #required bytes are available, then retry from the same position.
250|   *
251|   *    For example: A 1B buffer containing `0x19` (a 2B uint16 item) will
252|   *    set #required to 3 — the MTB byte plus two bytes of data.
253|   *
254|   *  - If the buffer was empty (source_size == 0), #required is set to 1
255|   *    since at least the initial MTB byte is needed.
256|   */
257|  size_t required;
258|};
